select cast(o.user_id as integer) as user_id, cast(l.product_id as integer) as product_id,
       cast(o.order_id as integer) as order_id, o.order_number, o.split,
       l.reordered, p.aisle_id, p.department_id
from "commerce"."staging"."stg_order_products" l
join "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_order_split" o using (order_id)
join "commerce"."staging"."stg_products" p using (product_id)

-- Global priors stay fixed at the training boundary for validation AND test.
with counts as (
    select product_id, count(*) as purchase_count, count(distinct user_id) as buyers,
           sum(reordered) as reorder_count
    from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_lines" where split = 'train' group by product_id
)
select p.*, coalesce(c.purchase_count, 0) as purchase_count, coalesce(c.buyers, 0) as buyers,
       coalesce(c.reorder_count, 0) as reorder_count
from "commerce"."staging"."stg_products" p left join counts c using (product_id)

select product_id
from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_product_prior"
where product_id is null

select
    product_id as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_product_prior"
where product_id is not null
group by product_id
having count(*) > 1

with actual as (
    select product_id,count(*) n from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_lines" where split='train' group by product_id
)
select p.product_id from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_product_prior" p left join actual a using(product_id)
where p.purchase_count != coalesce(a.n,0)

-- Test history adds the user's completed validation basket, never any test line.
with aggregated as (
    select user_id, product_id,
           count(*) filter (where split = 'train') as train_count,
           max(order_number) filter (where split = 'train') as train_last,
           sum(reordered) filter (where split = 'train') as train_reorders,
           count(*) as test_count, max(order_number) as test_last, sum(reordered) as test_reorders
    from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_lines" where split != 'test' group by user_id, product_id
)
select 'validation' as stage, user_id, product_id, train_count as purchase_count,
       train_last as last_order_number, train_reorders as reorder_count
from aggregated where train_count > 0
union all
select 'test', user_id, product_id, test_count, test_last, test_reorders from aggregated

select stage, user_id, product_id, count(*) as n
from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_history_product"
group by stage, user_id, product_id
having count(*) > 1

with order_history as (
    select user_id,
           count(*) filter (where split = 'train') as train_orders,
           max(order_number) filter (where split = 'train') as train_cutoff,
           count(*) as test_orders, max(order_number) as test_cutoff
    from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_order_split" where split != 'test' group by user_id
), products as (
    select stage, user_id, sum(purchase_count) as item_count, count(*) as unique_products
    from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_history_product" group by stage, user_id
)
select p.*, case when stage = 'validation' then train_orders else test_orders end as history_orders,
       case when stage = 'validation' then train_cutoff else test_cutoff end as cutoff_order_number
from products p join order_history using (user_id)

select stage, user_id, count(*) as n
from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_history_user"
group by stage, user_id
having count(*) > 1

with user_bounds as (
    select user_id,max(order_number) filter(where split='train') train_last,
           min(order_number) filter(where split='validation') validation_order,
           min(order_number) filter(where split='test') test_order,
           count(*) filter(where split='validation') validation_count,
           count(*) filter(where split='test') test_count
    from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_order_split" group by user_id
)
select cast(user_id as varchar) as invalid_key from user_bounds
where train_last >= validation_order or validation_order >= test_order
   or validation_count != 1 or test_count != 1
union all
select cast(h.user_id as varchar) from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_history_product" h
join "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_history_user" u using(stage,user_id)
where h.last_order_number > u.cutoff_order_number or h.purchase_count <= 0

-- Candidate-specific affinities are proportions of observed items, not held-out labels.
with counts as (
    select h.stage, h.user_id, p.aisle_id, p.department_id, sum(h.purchase_count) as n
    from "commerce"."recommendations"."rec_history_product" h join "commerce"."staging"."stg_products" p using (product_id)
    group by h.stage, h.user_id, p.aisle_id, p.department_id
)
select stage, user_id, 'aisle' as kind, aisle_id as category_id, sum(n) as item_count
from counts group by stage, user_id, aisle_id
union all
select stage, user_id, 'department', department_id, sum(n)
from counts group by stage, user_id, department_id
